{{Short description|German chemist}}{{Orphan|date=December 2024}}

'''Christian P. R. Hackenberger''' (b. Osnabruck, 1976) is a German chemist. He is a professor of Chemical Biology at the [[Humboldt University of Berlin]]<ref>{{Cite web |last= |title=Christian Hackenberger erhält Leibniz-Humboldt-Professur |url=https://www.hu-berlin.de/de/pr/nachrichten/archiv/nr1212/pm_121204_01 |access-date=2024-12-08 |website=Humboldt-UniversitÃ¤t zu Berlin |language=de}}</ref> and heads the research unit Biomolecule Modification and Delivery at the Leibniz Research Institute for Molecular Pharmacology.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-09-11 |title=Christian Hackenberger |url=https://leibniz-fmp.de/research/research-section/chemical-biology/christian-hackenberger-chemical-biology-ii |access-date=2024-12-08 |website=leibniz-fmp.de |language=en}}</ref> He is a co-founder of the Munich-based biotech company Tubulis.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Meet the Team behind Tubulis |url=https://tubulis.com/about/ |access-date=2024-12-08 |website=Tubulis |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Life and education ==
Christian Hackenberger grew up in [[Damme (Dümmer)|Damme]]. He attended the Gymnasium Damme, where he obtained his [[Abitur]] in 1995. After completing his civil service, he studied chemistry at the [[Albert-Ludwigs-Universität]] in [[Freiburg im Breisgau|Freiburg]] (1996–1998) and the [[University of Wisconsin–Madison|University of Wisconsin-Madison]] (M.S. with Samuel H. Gellman, 1998–1999), with support from the German Academic Scholarship Foundation.<ref>{{Cite web |title=90 Jahre, 90 Köpfe {{!}} Studienstiftung des deutschen Volkes |url=https://www.studienstiftung.de/90-jahre-90-koepfe/ |access-date=2024-12-08 |website=www.studienstiftung.de}}</ref> He pursued his doctoral studies at the [[RWTH Aachen University|RTWH Aachen]] (2000–2003), where he worked under Prof. Carsten Bolm as a Kekulé Fellow from the Fonds der Chemischen Industrie. During this time, he also worked as an editorial assistant in scientific journalism for the [[WDR Fernsehen|WDR]] broadcast "Quarks & Co". From 2003 to 2005 he was a [[DAAD Alumni Association of the US|DAAD]] Postdoctoral Fellow at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology under Prof. Barbara Imperiali.

In 2005, Hackenberger founded his own research group at the [[Free University of Berlin]] in 2005 as an [[Emmy Noether Program|Emmy Noether Fellow]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2010-11-11 |title=Dr. Christian Hackenberger Conducts Outstanding Research in Chemical Biology |url=https://www.fu-berlin.de/en/presse/informationen/fup/2010/fup_10_344/index.html |access-date=2024-12-08 |website=www.fu-berlin.de |language=en}}</ref> In 2011, he was appointed as W2 Professor of Bioorganic Chemistry at the Free University of Berlin as the first Plus 3 awardee from the Boehringer Ingelheim Foundation.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2010-11-11 |title=Christian Hackenberger überzeugt mit herausragender Forschung in der Chemischen Biologie |url=https://www.fu-berlin.de/presse/informationen/fup/2010/fup_10_344/index.html |access-date=2024-12-08 |website=www.fu-berlin.de |language=de}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Plus 3-Geförderte |url=https://www.boehringer-ingelheim-stiftung.de/was-wir-foerdern/foerdern-in-deutschland/perspektiven-programm-plus-3/plus-3-gefoerderte.html |access-date=2024-12-08 |website=www.boehringer-ingelheim-stiftung.de}}</ref> In 2012, he became Leibniz-Humboldt Professor for Chemical Biology at the Leibniz Research Institute for Molecular Pharmacology and the Humboldt University of Berlin. In 2020, Hackenberger co-founded the [[Munich]]-based biotechnology company Tubulis, which specializes in developing [[Antibody–drug conjugate|antibody-drug conjugates]]. He has served as associate editor of the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]]'s scientific journals [[Organic and Biomolecular Chemistry|O''rganic and Biomolecular Chemistry'']] (2015–2023) and ''[[Chemical Science (journal)|Chemical Science]]'' (since 2024).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Introducing OBC Associate Editor Prof. Christian Hackenberger – Organic & Biomolecular Chemistry Blog |url=https://blogs.rsc.org/ob/2015/05/27/introducing-obc-associate-editor-prof-christian-hackenberger/?doing_wp_cron=1733694839.1518259048461914062500 |access-date=2024-12-08 |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Chemical Science - The flagship journal of the Royal Society of Chemistry |url=https://www.rsc.org/journals-books-databases/about-journals/chemical-science/#editorial-board-tab |access-date=2024-12-08 |website=Royal Society of Chemistry |language=en-GB}}</ref> Hackenberger lives in [[Berlin]], and is married to the art historian Michel Otayek.

== Research ==
{{BLP unreferenced section|date=December 2024}}
Hackenberger's research at the Leibniz Research Institute focuses on chemical strategies to functionalize proteins and antibodies using highly selective chemical reactions to generate protein-based therapeutics against [[cancer]], [[Alzheimer's disease|Alzheimer's]] and [[Virus|viral]] [[Infection|infections]]. A particular focus of Hackenberger's research group is the engineering of new reactions for the modification and cellular delivery of [[Protein|proteins]] and [[Antibody|antibodies]] to advance their use in biological and pharmacological research.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-09-11 |title=Christian Hackenberger |url=https://leibniz-fmp.de/research/research-section/chemical-biology/christian-hackenberger-chemical-biology-ii |access-date=2025-02-03 |website=leibniz-fmp.de |language=en}}</ref> <!-- Contentious unsourced information removed per WP:BLP -->
